page.$description: Root screen canvas. Use for every screen's base background; not for cards, sheets, or modals.

surface.$description: Elevated container fill. Use for cards, bottom sheets, modals, dropdown menus, chat bubbles, toasts.

raised.$description: A surface sitting on top of another surface. Use when a card or row needs to separate from a container that is itself background.surface — the confirmed case is an optionRow inside a bottomSheet, where both would otherwise resolve to the same value and the row would vanish. Translucent on purpose so it composites correctly over any surface beneath it. Not a replacement for background.surface; only reach for it when there is a genuine second layer.

inverse.$description: Light fill for dark surfaces. Confirmed live use is status bar icon glyphs only; other uses unconfirmed.

scrim.$description: Semi-transparent overlay dimming content behind a modal.

floating.$description: Elevated floating surface with translucency, for dropdowns, tooltips, popovers.

stacking.$description: Additive white layer for stacking elevation on dark surfaces, e.g. toasts. RISK: resolves to the same value as interactive.secondary, interactive.disabled and interactive.pressed — coincidental, this token is a static elevation layer, not an interaction state, so the overlap is lower-risk here than for the other three.

input.$description: Fill of an editable field at rest; use text.primary for filled text, text.disabled for placeholders.

primary.$description: Main call-to-action fill. Max one interactive.primary button per screen.

primary:hover.$description: Hover state of interactive.primary, primary buttons only.

primary:active.$description: Pressed state of interactive.primary, primary buttons only.

secondary.$description: Supporting action fill: Skip, Cancel, filter chips, outlined buttons, toggles. RISK: resolves to the same value as interactive.disabled, background.stacking and interactive.pressed. Secondary and disabled are intentionally meant to read as equally quiet/receding — but if a secondary and a disabled control ever sit next to each other in the same view, a student has no color cue to tell them apart. Check that context before assuming this token alone carries the distinction.

destructive.$description: Irreversible harmful action fill: delete, remove, block buttons.

disabled.$description: Non-interactive control fill signaling unavailable. RISK: resolves to the same value as interactive.secondary, background.stacking and interactive.pressed. For this feature specifically: a mic button disabled by denied permission must not be visually confusable with an ordinary secondary button — pair this with text.disabled and consider whether disabled state needs a non-color signal (icon change, label) as well.

onDisabled.$description: Text and icons on interactive.disabled fills. Alias of text.disabled's value, kept in the interactive family so disabled controls (buttons, mic) don't reach into the text.* family for their icon/label color.

onPrimary.$description: Text and icons on interactive.primary fills; must contrast >= 4.5:1. Aliases navy.950 (16.6:1 on interactive.primary). Corrected 2026-09-16: this file said homie.inkwell (3.1:1), Figma has always said navy.950; Figma wins.

onSecondary.$description: Text and icons on interactive.secondary fills.

onDestructive.$description: Text and icons on interactive.destructive fills; must contrast >= 4.5:1.

pressed.$description: Semi-transparent tap-feedback overlay for light or vivid surfaces, when no dedicated :active token exists. Applied on top of the resting fill, never as a standalone background. RISK: of the four tokens sharing this value, this is the one most likely to need independent tuning later — it's a transient tap overlay, not a static surface. If contrast ever needs adjusting for it alone, split it into its own primitive rather than nudging alpha.light-10 and affecting the other three.

pressedInverse.$description: Semi-transparent tap-feedback overlay for dark surfaces, when no dedicated :active token exists.

primary.$description: Highest contrast text. Default when unsure which text token to pick.

secondary.$description: Reduced emphasis text: subtitles, captions, timestamps, helper text.

tertiary.$description: Lowest emphasis readable text: timestamps, counts, inline hints, eyebrow labels (hintCard "Hint", recallResult "You said"); not for anything a student must read to proceed. Was alpha.light-48 (4.2-4.3:1 on the dark surfaces it sits on); moved to light-52 on 2026-09-16 so 12px labels clear WCAG AA everywhere it is bound, while staying clearly under text.secondary (68%).

inverse.$description: Dark text on light or vivid surfaces; pair with background.inverse. Aliases navy.950. Corrected 2026-09-16: this file said homie.inkwell, Figma says navy.950; Figma wins.

link.$description: Inline hyperlink text only, not for buttons or nav items.

disabled.$description: Low-contrast text signaling unavailable or not yet filled.

success.$description: Confirmation text, e.g. "Correct"; not for use as a fill.

error.$description: Validation message text under a failed field.

warning.$description: Caution text: limits, expiry notices, "one attempt left".

onAccent.$description: Text on any accent.*.bold fill; must contrast >= 4.5:1 against that accent.

default.$description: Standard container edge: card outlines, dividers, input borders at rest.

subtle.$description: An edge quieter than border.default but stronger than nothing, for the middle of a graduated set. Confirmed consumer: the second of the three listening pulse rings, which previously reached past the semantic layer to alpha.light-18 because no token sat between default and strong.

strong.$description: Higher contrast container edge for dividers that must read at a glance, table rules.

focus.$description: Keyboard focus ring; pair with Stroke/Heavy Border at 2px, never remove without replacement.

error.$description: Invalid input edge; pair with text.error underneath.

success.$description: Validated input edge for fields confirmed correct.

selected.$description: Edge of a chosen element; pair with highlight.surface as the fill.

surface.$description: Fill of a chosen element: selected cards, active tabs, the answer a student picked.

border.$description: Edge of a chosen element, paired with highlight.surface, never alone.

surface-hover.$description: Hover state on a selected card. Unconfirmed against a live screen; gated on highlight.surface's own applicability to this feature.

surface-pressed.$description: Full press feedback on a selected card. Unconfirmed against a live screen; gated on highlight.surface's own applicability to this feature.

signature.$description: Mascot signature violet, a character color. Only use when the Homie mascot is conceptually present on screen.

eyes.$description: Homie eye whites, mascot illustration only.

bold.$description: Solid green accent fill: streak counters, progress markers, positive stat chips. Not for validation success. Confirmed real consumer: statChip's Score variant border/text/icon, verified as a genuine variable binding (not hardcoded hex) as of the Fifth pass.

subtle.$description: Low emphasis green fill: tinted background behind a green stat or chip.

bold.$description: Solid coral accent fill: decorative emphasis, category tags, illustration accents. Not for errors.

Solid blue accent fill: informational chips, secondary category tags. Not for links. Confirmed real consumer: statChip's XP variant border/text/icon, verified as a genuine variable binding (not hardcoded hex) as of the Fifth pass.

Solid magenta accent fill: decorative category tags. Confirmed real consumer: statChip's Time variant border/text/icon, a stand-in for a true purple/violet accent that doesn't exist yet in this layer, imperfect but deliberate, see design-system notes. Verified as a genuine variable binding (not hardcoded hex) as of the Fifth pass; move this variant to a real violet accent if one is ever added.
Solid brand violet fill: brand moments, onboarding hero panels. Not for primary CTAs.

subtle.$description: Low emphasis brand fill: tinted brand panels.

bold.$description: Solid PRO fill: PRO badges, upgrade banners. Not for warnings.

accent.$description: Alias of pro.bold, kept for an older naming convention. Use for PRO badges and upgrade prompts.

bold.$description: Solid success fill: correct answer banners, completion states. Not for decorative green.

subtle.$description: Tinted success background, the panel behind a correct result.

bold.$description: Solid error fill: incorrect answer banners, failed validation summaries. Not for destructive buttons.

subtle.$description: Tinted error background, the panel behind a wrong result.

bold.$description: Solid tag fill for a couldn't-hear or ambiguous-input result. Parallels feedback.success.bold and feedback.error.bold, same structure, third verdict.

subtle.$description: Tinted background if a full card treatment is ever needed for this state.

bold.$description: Solid fill for a due-or-caution-adjacent marker that isn't a verdict. Confirmed consumer: the 'Hint used' indicator on a recall result, distinct from the Pass/Partial/Miss verdict itself (which uses feedback.success/error), this marks how an answer was reached, not whether it was right. Parallels feedback.success.bold/feedback.error.bold/feedback.unclear.bold in structure, fourth entry in the same family.

border.$description: Outline for a due-or-caution element that is bordered rather than filled. Confirmed consumers: swipeChip on the plan-active home, where an amber border signals an approaching deadline without the weight of a solid fill, and dueSignalCard, which previously carried a raw hex for the same job. Currently the same value as feedback.warning.bold by design; split so a bordered treatment can move independently of a filled one.

subtle.$description: Tinted background if a full card treatment is ever needed for this state.

onSubtle.$description: Text and icons on feedback.warning.subtle. Same value text.warning already uses standalone.

md.$description: 18px. Headline XS and Body M, both weights.

wide.$description: +8%. Uppercase eyebrow labels only (LISTENING, bucket headings, picker group labels). Added 2026-09-21: three files were writing calc(tracking.loose * 0.08em), which names a 1% token and renders 8%, so retuning loose would have moved them eightfold.

tight.$description: -1%. Display sizes and Headline L and above.

loose.$description: +1%. Headline XS and below, all Body, all Caption.

display.$description: Used for Display L only. Greed Condensed. Figma's Display L style binds here (rebound 2026-09-16; it had been on fontFamily.default). In code the family is the single Greed VF and Condensed is expressed as typography.primitive.fontWidth.condensed on the wdth axis; the name here mirrors Figma, it is not used as a CSS family.

default.$description: Used for every text style except Display L. RESOLVED 2026-09-16: Greed, no substitute. Since 2026-09-16 loaded as one variable file, Greed VF (wght 300-900, wdth 75-130), from src/app/fonts/ via next/font/local as --font-greed; the page pins wdth to 100 (Standard). Overrides the Platform Constraints substitution rule on purpose.

condensed.$description: 75%. Greed VF wdth axis, the Condensed cut. Display L only. Applied as font-stretch.

standard.$description: 100%. Greed VF wdth axis, the Standard cut. The page default; every text style except Display L.

regular.$description: Body copy and the Regular variants of Headline XS and XXS.

semibold.$description: The Bold-labeled variants of Headline XS/XXS, Body and Caption.

bold.$description: Display M and S, Headline XL through S.

heavy.$description: Display L only, paired with fontFamily.display. On the Greed VF this is wght 900 (the file's own 'Heavy' instance), not 800.

displayL.$description: Largest display size, Condensed Heavy: fontFamily.display (Greed Condensed in Figma) with fontWidth.condensed (wdth 75) and fontWeight.heavy (900) on the VF in code. Applied 2026-09-16.

displayM.$description: Display size for hero numeric moments, e.g. session stats.

bodyMRegular.$description: Medium body copy, regular weight. Default body text.

captionSBold.$description: Smallest caption, bold weight. Below the Platform Constraints' 11px caption minimum — sits at 9px per the file's own token, same as captionSRegular. Flag before using this for anything a student needs to actually read; fine for decorative or redundant labels only.

captionSRegular.$description: Smallest caption, regular weight. Below the Platform Constraints' 11px caption minimum only if used at raw size; here it sits at 9px per the file's own token.

150.$description: 150ms. Micro-feedback: button press, checkbox toggle, mic circle press-down.

250.$description: 250ms. State transitions: idle to recording, processing to result.

300.$description: 300ms. Swipe-to-settle for a card carousel. UNCONFIRMED: matched to common iOS carousel timing, not verified against a reference or a prototype — the same epistemic status as the +10 XP value. Tune once the swipe is prototyped.

1100.$description: 1100ms, loops. Mic-pulse timing, matched to iOS dictation / WhatsApp voice-note comparables.

fast.$description: Micro-feedback timing: button press, checkbox toggle, the mic circle's press-down scale.

standard.$description: State transitions: idle to recording, processing to result, the Voice UX Reference's Must-state beats.

swipe.$description: Card-to-card transition when the student swipes between due quizzes on the plan-active home. Longer than standard because the card travels a full screen-width and the count badge and dots update with it; the motion has to read as one continuous movement, not a state flip.

ambient.$description: Looping ambient timing, e.g. the mic listening-state pulse.

standard.$description: The curve fast, standard and ambient durations all use.

mobile.$description: deviceWidth at the mobile breakpoint. Part of a 3-mode collection (Desktop/Mobile/Tablet); DTCG has no native mode support so each mode is a sibling token. Figma's Responsive collection was updated to 390 the same day; the two are in sync.

rootFontSize.$description: Browser root font size, same across all three modes. References typography.primitive.fontSize.root.

screenMargin.$description: Standard horizontal screen margin, 16px, matches the platform constraints doc exactly.

cardPadding.$description: Interior padding for cards, sheets and the recall turn bubble. Shares its value with screenMargin by design, same base padding unit.

betweenSections.$description: Vertical gap between major blocks on a screen, e.g. between the prompt bubble and the mic control.

cardLabelGap.$description: Vertical gap between a card's own label or title and its body text. chatBubble's title-to-body gap, hintCard's label-to-body gap. Not for gaps between separate blocks on a screen, that's betweenSections.

tapTarget.$description: Minimum height of any tappable control's hit area, 48px. A literal, not a spacing step: it is the touch-target floor, not a layout rhythm value. button's outer frame binds its min-height here on every size; the visible pill inside can be shorter (see component.button).

component.$description: Component tokens exist only when a component's bindings actually branch by state or variant in a way that benefits from its own indirection layer between it and the semantic tokens, not as documentation-only aliases for a value that never changes. micButton is the only entry here on purpose: its four states each pair with a different semantic token, and these tokens are the real thing its Figma variables are bound to, not a restatement of them. chatBubble and hintCard never branch, they bind straight to semantic tokens with nothing in between, so a component.chatBubble.* or component.hintCard.* entry here would just be a second name for a value already named once. optionRow does branch by state the same way micButton does, four variants, four different fills, but its Figma variants bind straight to the semantic tokens directly rather than through a component-specific layer. That's an inconsistency with micButton's pattern, not a mistake exactly, treat micButton's indirection layer as the older, legacy approach rather than the template: an indirection layer that never diverges from what it aliases is upkeep with no payoff. Don't add one to a new component by default. Add one only when there's a concrete reason a component's own token might need to move independently of the semantic token it currently matches.

button.$description: Heights of button's visible pill per size. These were fixed, unbound numbers in Figma until 2026-09-16; now bound there and here. Literal values because 56 has no primitive and 32/40 only coincide with icon/illustration steps that mean something else. The outer hit area is spacing.semantic.tapTarget, not these.

height.$description: Size S pill height. Inside a 48px tap target (spacing.semantic.tapTarget).
Size M pill height. Inside a 48px tap target (spacing.semantic.tapTarget).
Size L pill height. Taller than the tap target, so the pill is the hit area.

scaffold.$description: Region heights for the screen scaffold every screen is built on. Unlike micButton's entries these are not an indirection layer over a semantic token — there is no semantic token for them, and no primitive genuinely matches: 48 is not a spacing step, 56 is another component's pill height, 120 is not an illustration box, and 34 has no primitive at all. Stated as literals on purpose rather than aliased to a near-value that means something else, which is the mislabelled-binding mistake this file has been caught by before. The namespace is earned by the React ScreenShell component, not by Figma bindings: scaffold itself is an external team-library component and its variables will never route through this file. Only middleContent has no entry — it flexes to fill whatever the four fixed regions leave, so at an 844-tall viewport it computes to 620 and matches the Figma frames, and at any other height it absorbs the difference.

height.$description: Status-bar region at the top of every screen. A literal: 48 here is the iOS status-bar area, unrelated to size.primitive.space.1200 (a spacing step) or spacing.semantic.tapTarget (a hit-area floor, which its own description says is not a layout rhythm value).
Region holding the appBar and the session fraction. A literal: component.button.l.height is also 56, but aliasing across components is how a value silently changes for the wrong reason.

The action zone at the foot of a screen. A literal: size.primitive.illustration.1500 is also 120, but that is an illustration box and a footer region is not one. component.micButton.diameter does alias it, legitimately, because a micButton genuinely is a 120 illustration-sized circle.
Home-indicator region, and the slot a bottom sheet occupies on its own branch screen. No primitive of this value exists.

stroke.$description: Idle mic circle outline. border.strong: the Figma Idle frame had always rendered at this value, bound to border/strong directly; rebound through this token 2026-09-16 (the token had said border.default).

fill.$description: Listening mic circle fill; the pulsing ring on top is additive motion, not load-bearing, so it still reads with reduced motion on.

glyph.$description: Captured mic circle icon color. Same fill as captured.fill (brand.bold), so it takes the same contrast pairing as listening.glyph.

fill.$description: Paused mic circle fill. Added 2026-09-21 after a render check found Listening and Paused identical: the control kept the listening fill and the pulse ring kept animating while the caption said stopped. A paused recorder must not look like a running one.

glyph.$description: Paused mic circle icon colour, on the quieter paused fill.

fill.$description: Disabled mic circle fill, for permission-denied or mic-unavailable states.

glyph.$description: Disabled mic circle icon color, for permission-denied or mic-unavailable states.

pulse.$description: The three listening-state pulse rings around the mic. In Figma these are loose ELLIPSE siblings of the recording screen, not children of it, which is how all three came to be present, positioned and invisible at once — buried in z-order. Sized here so the React version can parent them to the mic and make that failure impossible. Stated as literals: no primitive genuinely matches. illustration.2500 is also 200, but a pulse ring is not an illustration box, and aliasing to a near-value that means something else is the mislabelled-binding mistake this file has been caught by before.

ringInner.$description: Innermost pulse ring, 40 outside the 120 mic circle.

ringOuter.$description: Outermost pulse ring, twice the mic diameter.

diameter.$description: Mic circle diameter, the primary tap target in the recall loop.

size.$description: Mic glyph box inside the 120px circle. A literal, bound in Figma on every state's glyph frame; no primitive of the right kind is 48 (tapTarget is a hit-area rule, not an icon size).
